indices.subtitle: Basic covers index notation, powers, squares and square and cube roots, prime factors and factor trees, and the first index laws with the zero index. Expected adds prime factorisation in index form, HCF and LCM, estimating roots, order of operations, showing why the index laws work, and the index laws with pronumerals.

ratios-rates.subtitle: Basic covers simplifying and equivalent ratios, a ratio as a fraction, sharing in a ratio, unit rates and reading and drawing distance–time graphs. Expected adds ratios with units, three-part ratios, ratio problems from one part or a difference, scale, converting rates, best buys, speed, distance and time, and drawing and interpreting distance–time graphs with a return journey.

linear.subtitle: Basic covers reading and plotting points and quadrants, tables of values, matching rules, completing a table and drawing the line, and solving an equation by drawing graphs. Expected adds rules from tables and graphs, patterns, real-life relationships, lines in all four quadrants, and graphical solutions and points of intersection.

area.subtitle: Basic covers rectangles, triangles and parallelograms (including drawing shapes with a given area), missing lengths, the area of a circle in terms of π and choosing units. Expected adds trapeziums (and why the formula works), rhombuses and kites, circles, sectors, semicircles and quadrants, composite shapes, working backwards and converting units of area.

volume.subtitle: Basic covers views of solids (choose and draw), prisms, counting cubes, V = Ah, rectangular prisms and units of volume and capacity. Expected adds drawing top, front and side views, triangular, trapezium and composite prisms, cylinders, missing dimensions, capacity and converting units.

geometrical-figures.subtitle: Basic covers classifying and sketching triangles and quadrilaterals, their properties, and the angle sums of triangles and quadrilaterals. Expected adds classifying by sides and angles together, which triangles are possible, isosceles and exterior angles, the quadrilateral family, convex and non-convex polygons, and angles and sides found from properties.

data-visualisation.subtitle: Basic covers categorical and numerical data, frequency tables, drawing column graphs and dot plots, and reading column graphs, dot plots, pictograms and line graphs. Expected adds classifying variables fully, census, sample and bias, choosing a display, drawing stem-and-leaf plots and histograms, and reading stem-and-leaf plots, histograms, sector and divided bar graphs and misleading graphs.

data-analysis.subtitle: Basic covers the mean, median, mode and range (alone and together), the mean in context, the effect of a new value, and statistics from a dot plot. Expected adds even-sized data sets, the mean to 1 decimal place, missing values, outliers and changing data, frequency tables, stem-and-leaf plots, the shape of a distribution, comparing data sets and choosing a measure of centre.

probability.subtitle: Basic covers chance words, the 0 to 1 scale, sample spaces, dice, spinners, bags and cards, and P(A) with P(not A). Expected adds probabilities as fractions, decimals and percentages, letters, outcomes that are not equally likely, relative frequency (and explaining it), expected numbers and complementary events.

pythagoras.subtitle: Basic covers the hypotenuse, writing Pythagoras' theorem, squares and square roots, testing for a right angle, and finding the hypotenuse (with and without a diagram). Expected adds Pythagorean triads, answers to 1 decimal place, shorter sides, mixed units, isosceles triangles and problems in context where students draw the diagram.

angle-relationships.subtitle: Basic covers classifying and naming angles, reading a protractor, angles in a right angle, on a straight line and around a point, vertically opposite angles, and complementary and supplementary angles. Expected adds reflex angles, angle pairs on parallel lines (naming them, finding angles, and deciding whether lines are parallel), and multi-step problems and equations with reasons.

integers.subtitle: Basic covers integers on a number line, comparing and ordering, thermometers, adding and subtracting, multiplying and dividing, and problems in context. Expected adds why a negative times a negative is positive, chains of multiplication and division, order of operations, substitution with negatives, reasoning (true or false, spot the error) and multi-part problems.

equations.subtitle: Basic covers representing equations, balances and bar models, solving by inspection, one-step and two-step equations, word problems, checking by substitution and solving x² = c. Expected adds fraction and bracket equations, collecting like terms, pronumerals on both sides, equivalent equations, formulas, form-solve-check, spotting errors, multi-step word problems and ax² = c.

fdp.subtitle: Basic covers equivalent and simplified fractions, comparing, rounding, terminating and recurring decimals, conversions, rational and irrational numbers, ordering, adding and subtracting, fractions of quantities and sets, and percentages of quantities. Expected adds mixed numbers, multiplying and dividing fractions and decimals, one quantity as a percentage of another, percentage change, discounts, GST, profit and loss, reverse percentages, the double number line and reasoning.

s3-whole-numbers.topic: Represents Numbers: Whole Numbers and Integers
s3-whole-numbers.subtitle: Part A: recognise, represent and order numbers in the millions; apply place value to partition, regroup and rename numbers to 1 billion. Parts A and B add: locate and represent integers on a number line.

s3-decimals.subtitle: Part A: recognise that the place value system can be extended beyond hundredths; compare, order and represent decimals.

s3-percentages.subtitle: Part B: make connections between benchmark fractions, decimals and percentages; determine percentage discounts of 10%, 25% and 50%.

s3-additive.subtitle: Part A: apply efficient mental and written strategies to solve addition and subtraction problems; use estimation and place value understanding to determine the reasonableness of solutions. Parts A and B add: choose and use efficient strategies to solve addition and subtraction problems; applies known strategies to add and subtract decimals.

s3-multiply-divide.subtitle: Part A: determine products and factors; use partitioning and place value to multiply 2-, 3- and 4-digit numbers by one-digit numbers; select and apply mental and written strategies to multiply 2- and 3-digit numbers by 2-digit numbers; represent and solve division problems with whole number remainders; select and apply strategies to divide a number with 3 or more digits by a one-digit divisor; use estimation and rounding to check the reasonableness of answers to calculations. Parts A and B add: select and apply strategies to solve problems involving multiplication and division with whole numbers; multiply and divide decimals by powers of 10.

s3-number-sentences.topic: Multiplicative Relations: Number Sentences and Patterns
s3-number-sentences.subtitle: Part B: use equivalent number sentences involving multiplication and division to find unknown quantities; represent and describe number patterns formed by multiples; explore the use of brackets and the order of operations to write number sentences.

s3-fractions.subtitle: Part A: recognise the role of the number 1 as representing the whole; compare and order common unit fractions; solve problems involving addition and subtraction of fractions with the same denominator. Parts A and B add: recognise that a fraction can represent a division; compare common fractions with related denominators; use equivalence to add and subtract fractional quantities.

s3-fraction-quantities.subtitle: Part B: build up to the whole from a given fractional part; find fractional quantities of whole numbers (halves, quarters, fifths and tenths).

s3-position.subtitle: Part A: explore the Cartesian coordinate system. Parts A and B add: use the 4 quadrants of the coordinate plane.

s3-length.subtitle: Part A: use metres and kilometres for length and distances; measure lengths to find perimeters. Parts A and B add: connect decimal representations to the metric system; convert between common metric units of length; solve problems involving the comparison of lengths using appropriate units.

s3-angles.subtitle: Part A: estimate, measure and compare angles using degrees; use a protractor to measure and identify types of angles. Parts A and B add: investigate angles on a straight line and angles at a point; investigate the relationships formed by the intersection of straight lines.

s3-2d-shapes.subtitle: Part A: classify two-dimensional shapes and describe their properties. Parts A and B add: dissect two-dimensional shapes and rearrange them using translations, reflections and rotations.

s3-area-rectangles.subtitle: Part A: use hectares and square kilometres as units of measurement for area; calculate the areas of rectangles using familiar metric units.

s3-area-composite.topic: 2D Spatial Structure: Area of Composite Figures, Parallelograms and Triangles
s3-area-composite.subtitle: Part B: find the area of composite figures; calculate the area of a parallelogram using subdivision and rearrangement; determine the area of a triangle.

s3-3d-objects.subtitle: Part A: compare, describe and name prisms and pyramids; connect three-dimensional objects with two-dimensional representations. Parts A and B add: construct prisms and pyramids.

s3-volume-capacity.subtitle: Part A: choose appropriate units of measurement for capacity; use displacement to investigate volumes of irregular solids; connect decimal representations to the metric system. Parts A and B add: use cubic metres for measurement of volume; recognise the multiplicative structure for finding volume; find the volumes of rectangular prisms in cubic centimetres and cubic metres.

s3-mass.subtitle: Part A: choose appropriate units of measurement for mass; connect decimal representations to the metric system. Parts A and B add: convert between common metric units of mass.

s3-time.subtitle: Part A: compare 12- and 24-hour time systems and convert between them. Parts A and B add: solve problems involving duration, using 12- and 24-hour time.

s3-data-collect.subtitle: Part A: collect categorical and discrete numerical data by observation or survey; choose and use appropriate tables and graphs.

s3-data-interpret.subtitle: Part A: describe and interpret different datasets in context. Parts A and B add: interpret and compare a range of data displays; interpret data presented in digital media and elsewhere.

s3-chance.subtitle: Part A: list outcomes of chance experiments involving equally likely outcomes and represent probabilities. Parts A and B add: compare observed frequencies of outcomes with expected results; create random generators and describe probabilities using fractions; conduct chance experiments with both small and large numbers of trials.

length.subtitle: Basic covers the perimeter of parallelograms, trapeziums, rhombuses, kites and composite figures, the parts of a circle and the circumference from the radius or diameter. Expected adds composite figures with sides to find, arc length, the perimeter of sectors, semicircles and quadrants, composite figures with curves, and working backwards from a circumference.

algebraic-techniques.subtitle: Basic covers coefficients, pronumerals and constants, algebraic notation, writing expressions from words, one-step substitution, collecting like terms, multiplying and dividing a term, expanding a bracket and factorising out a number. Expected adds tables of values, multi-step expressions from words, two-step substitution and substitution with two pronumerals, mixed like terms, multiplying terms, algebraic fractions, expanding and simplifying, and factorising with negatives, two pronumerals and three terms.
